<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-008 -->
# R0008: Round-trip valid simulated wall times through timezone transitions

**Repository-local identity:** `R0008` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#8](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-008. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #8. Proposed priority P2; instrument/acceptance defect with an existing hourly-weather consumer. This main-based work order specifies the repair and its limits; it authorizes neither implementation nor publication.

## The witnessed failure and why one offset is insufficient

For configured zone `America/New_York`, the actual `epochForTzTime(2026,3,8,3,30)` returned `2026-03-08T08:30:00.000Z` on main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624` and candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`. Formatting that result back through the actual zone helper yielded **04:30**, although the requested valid local time was **03:30**. The independent expected instant is `2026-03-08T07:30:00.000Z`. DATE-013 captured this with exact source fragments in a Node VM and controlled environment, not in a browser or live provider request.

The function makes a UTC guess for local fields, observes the zone offset at that guess, and corrects once. On the transition day, that offset belongs to the other side of the change. Nothing checks whether the result still has the requested local fields. A finite output therefore passed an invalid scene to its consumers. The candidate retains this defect; it is evidence, not an assumed implementation target.

This is separate from subtracting prayer wall minutes across DST ([R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7)) and default clock corrections ([R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32)). It is also not simulation-only: the existing hourly-weather parser invokes the same helper for every returned wall-time string. [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) must pass its captured request zone rather than the global zone selected later. `tomorrowStr()` already passed the saved civil month/year/leap/DST controls; its calendar increment is not replaced here.

## Re-anchor source, then keep the interface small

Before future mutation, record `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html tests/smoke.html DESIGN.md`, using the same `git -C` prefix. Stop for relevant incompatible drift. Main is the repair baseline; neither the audit branch nor an arbitrary future HEAD inherits a defect assertion without checking its current functions.

Owned source is [the temporal helpers and simulation initialization](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L699-L731), with the [existing hourly caller](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L795-L799), [boot's early celestial reads](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2182-L2186), [error presentation](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1193), and [simulation readout](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2032-L2034). The comparison is [candidate conversion/init](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L725-L728).

Choose the numeric compatibility interface explicitly:

```text
epochForTzTime(y,mo,d,h,mi,zone=tz) -> finite epoch milliseconds | NaN
finite: exactly one supported inverse matches every requested field
NaN: invalid date/zone, unsupported representation, no inverse, or multiple inverses
```

The configured-zone default remains only for intentional synchronous configuration callers. Async weather must pass the sixth argument. This introduces no persisted schema, provider field or new public configuration option. `NaN` is an internal unavailable signal: every consumer must branch before formatting, subtracting, adopting a simulation anchor or using an epoch as freshness evidence. Do not expose NaN in the UI or let `new Date(NaN)` cascade through the model.

## Concrete bounded inverse, with a declared precision boundary

Use the browser's existing Intl timezone data; do not infer offsets from three samples and claim all IANA history. The selected repair uses a **bounded exhaustive index of minute-aligned instants for one civil day**, reused by the existing callers. This matches the widget's `HH:mm` input precision while allowing both fold candidates to be found. It is a specific implementation design, not executed code or a universal timezone theorem.

The supported representation is a Gregorian date, integer hour/minute, second zero, an Intl-supported zone, and whole-minute UTC offsets within ±24 hours throughout the inspected window. Reject invalid Gregorian fields instead of allowing Date to normalize February 30; reject nonfinite fields, hours outside 0–23, minutes outside 0–59, and unusable zones. Years must be positive finite integers representable by Date and Intl. Use a UTC date constructor based on `setUTCFullYear` when validating years 1–99 so Date.UTC's special 1900 interpretation cannot change the requested year. Project with an explicitly Gregorian, Latin-digit, h23 formatter; do not accept the existing `partsInTz` catch-to-device-zone fallback as a successful inversion.

The exact algorithm is:

1. Let `U` be the strict UTC representation of the requested civil **date at 00:00**, used only as a search coordinate. Construct one formatter for the explicitly supplied zone. Make a 1440-entry table for the target day's local minute; entries initially contain no epochs.
2. Visit UTC epoch minutes from `U-86400000` through `U+172800000`, inclusive, in increments of 60000: at most **4321 projections**. This is the entire possible epoch window for a target-day minute when offset magnitude is at most 24 hours. It does not choose a few representative offsets.
3. For each projection, validate numeric Gregorian parts and compute the represented offset from its full year/month/day/hour/minute/second fields relative to the projected UTC epoch. If formatting fails, the projected offset is nonfinite/outside the bound, or it is not an integral number of minutes, mark this day profile unsupported and return no valid conversions from it. Do not silently round seconds offsets into minutes. For projections whose local date equals the target date and whose seconds are zero, append the epoch to the matching local-minute entry, deduplicating exact equal epochs.
4. Read entry `h*60+mi`. Zero epochs means unavailable (a gap is one possible cause); two or more means ambiguous; both return NaN. One epoch is accepted only after a final strict projection equality check of year, month, day, hour, minute and second zero. A gap never slides forward and a fold never chooses whichever offset happened to be visited first.
5. Keep at most four in-memory day profiles keyed by exact `(zone,y,mo,d)` with simple eviction. Cache unsupported profiles too, so a bad clock is not rescanned every frame. Reuse one profile for all hourly records on that day and for simulation/countdown consumers. No localStorage entry, location-generation field, global scheduler or new dependency is introduced. Configuration changes cannot change the meaning of a key because the zone is part of it; async ownership of results remains a separate gate.

For this minute-aligned domain, every possible epoch for an input local minute is included in the finite window; uniqueness is checked across that domain rather than assumed from convergence. Non-minute historical offsets and other unsupported representations must fail closed when the profile detects them. This does **not** promise exhaustive second-resolution historical timezone support or correctness for exotic transition behavior outside the stated representation. A caller needing such historical support requires a separately justified resolver/data contract; it may not treat this repair's tested current-provider/date cases as a universal certification. Do not claim arbitrary IANA history is supported merely because one case returned a number.

The cost is deliberately bounded and paid per zone/day, not per frame or hourly element. A profile cache without real callers is insufficient, and rebuilding it for each of 72 hourly strings is a regression. Future browser qualification must record profile-build count and actual responsiveness on the widget's supported host. If the bounded cold-build cost is unacceptable there, stop before acceptance; do not replace exhaustive coverage with sparse samples and keep the same claim. No unmeasured millisecond performance guarantee is part of this work order.

## Wire validity into actual consumers

Integrate in this order: strict inverse and its profile reuse; simulation initialization/error boundaries; captured-zone hourly caller through its owner; elapsed-countdown caller through its owner; then combined acceptance.

- `initSim` assigns `_simBase`, `_rafT0` and `_simTz` only after the requested explicit simulation time resolves. Preserve the existing valid hour/minute parsing behavior before conversion; this issue does not justify an unrelated query-parser redesign. If the parsed fields are outside the converter domain or yield no unique instant, record an explicit simulation-invalid state and do not retain an older anchor as if it were the new requested scene.
- Guard explicit-scene initialization **before** the first clock-dependent `buildStars`/`renderMoon` work in `boot`, before reset/config scene work, and after an eligible provider-zone adoption would reinitialize the scene. On invalid explicit simulation, use the existing error presentation with `.nt="—"` and `.left="Simulation time unavailable"`; set the existing `.simclock` text to `SIM unavailable` and show it. Do not run that scene's model, cloud/star/moon time projection or loop day-fetch branch with an invalid epoch. Keep the fixed card/header/footer/settings geometry and permit a valid configuration/reload to initialize normally. An invalid configured-zone scene stays explicitly unavailable; do not silently pretend it is the live clock or a different wall time. An omitted/incorrect zone hint that makes an explicit preview unresolved is not a promise that the eventual location scene has been verified; supply a valid existing `tz` hint or reload with a valid time to qualify that scene. Ordinary loads without explicit simTime are not blocked by this inverse failure path.
- A failure after a previously valid zone/scene must also invalidate its visible clock-dependent output; a generic error string followed by the next unconditional render of the old scene is a false repair. At the high-level boot/apply/loop boundaries, branch on simulation validity before clock use. Keep validity handling local to these existing entry points rather than add exceptions to every atmospheric formula. No rejected scene is credited as a normal moonless night or a motion-qualified preview.
- [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) owns capture and propagation of `requestZone` to the existing hourly parser. Check request ownership before committing, and compute hourly epochs with this sixth argument, never by temporarily changing global `tz`. If any required track time is invalid/ambiguous, reject that candidate track as usable interpolation/age evidence rather than sorting NaNs or silently shifting it; admitted current observed weather can remain independently usable under its own validation/freshness rules. The source-age qualification consumer is [R000B](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/11).
- [R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7) uses `Number.isFinite` on the converter result before elapsed subtraction. Unresolved endpoints produce its exact `Countdown unavailable` output, not an approximate duration. No provider fold disambiguation has been established from a bare HH:mm string, so no arbitrary earlier/later policy is added here.

Using another one-offset helper for weather or countdown would recreate disagreement between consumers. Abandoning all DST inputs would avoid the witness by removing valid functionality. Returning the first fold match gives unsupported precision. Adding a timezone dependency, changing the provider to avoid the contract, or redesigning the simulation UI is unnecessary for this bounded repair.

## Public RED and deterministic acceptance

The following is a **proposed public source fixture**, not a newly executed result. Run it only against the selected isolated source tree. Its expected instant is literal and independent of the converter. It executes the real temporal block, rather than an imitation helper; adjust extraction markers only if verified final-source placement changes and retain the extracted text/hash in the test receipt.

```js
const fs = require('node:fs'), vm = require('node:vm');
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const src = fs.readFileSync('index.html', 'utf8');
const a = src.indexOf('const _RAFNOW =');
const b = src.indexOf('// ---- prayer-times data:', a);
assert(a >= 0 && b > a);
const c = vm.createContext({Intl, Date, URLSearchParams,
  q: new URLSearchParams(''), SIM: {time:null}, tz:'America/New_York',
  performance:{now:()=>0}, pad:n=>String(n).padStart(2,'0')});
vm.runInContext(src.slice(a,b), c);
const epoch = vm.runInContext('epochForTzTime(2026,3,8,3,30)', c,
                              {timeout:5000});
assert.equal(epoch, Date.parse('2026-03-08T07:30:00.000Z'));
```

The preserved baseline result is 08:30Z, so the assertion is RED there. The 5000 ms fixture guard contains an unexpected loop; it is not a claimed production deadline or measured runtime. Add the matrix below using the same actual helper and explicit sixth argument. Formatting expected values must not call the implementation under test.

| Input | Expected output/control |
|---|---|
| New York 2026-03-08 03:30 | 07:30Z; final local fields exactly 03:30. |
| New York 2026-03-08 01:30 | 06:30Z; valid pre-transition control. |
| New York 2026-09-07 03:30 | 07:30Z; ordinary-day control. |
| New York 2026-03-08 02:30 | NaN; no valid requested wall minute, no shifted 03:30. |
| New York 2026-11-01 01:30 | NaN; entries contain both 05:30Z and 06:30Z. |
| New York 2026-11-01 03:30 | 08:30Z; valid post-fold control. |
| Kathmandu 2026-09-07 03:30 | `2026-09-06T21:45:00.000Z`; fractional offset and prior UTC date. |
| UTC 2024-02-29 00:00; invalid 2026-02-30 | Valid leap day resolves exactly; invalid date is NaN without normalization. |
| Invalid IANA zone, nonfinite fields, hour 24, minute 60 | NaN and no device-zone fallback. |
| Isolated formatter fixture exposes a 30-second offset or offset outside ±24h | Unsupported profile, NaN; do not round it. This is a synthetic unsupported-representation control, not a factual claim about a named zone. |

Combined accepted interface fixture: hold hourly string `2026-03-08T03:30` from a New York request, change global config to Riyadh, then complete. Pure conversion using captured New York zone is 07:30Z, neither historical 08:30Z nor a Riyadh-derived epoch. Obsolete generation cannot commit even a correctly converted track; equivalent current-generation control can. A fold/gap track is unavailable to source-age qualification. This combined fixture was planned in the accepted relationship refinement; it is not a new historical PASS.

Consumer controls must include frozen valid simTime, accelerated scale, settled-zone reinitialization, invalid explicit-scene error before first celestial render, and invalid→valid reload/config recovery. In the actual browser, observe the requested clock text, error/readiness state and rendered scene; do not change the OS clock or equate a finite helper result with a qualified picture. Keep default real-time motion/reduced-motion controls, opaque moon and readable 325×530 layout on valid scenes. Record profile builds for repeated same-day hourly/model calls; bounded cache reuse must be observable.

In authorized disposable mutation fixtures, restore the single-offset implementation, choose the first fold entry, remove explicit-zone propagation, and bypass the invalid consumer branch separately. Each corresponding case must fail. Restore the final tree before acceptance. Existing invalid-date behavior in unrelated `partsInTz` callers is a regression control; narrowing the inverse must not globally replace that helper's fallback semantics without separate caller evidence.

## Ownership, rollback and closure

Preserve [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8) → [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) for explicit-zone conversion semantics/captured hourly caller, the conversion interface consumed by [R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7), and source-epoch qualification in [R000B](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/11). Coordinate clock-mode writes with [R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32). One integrator owns overlapping converter/caller and simulation-entry hunks; this adds no directed edge or whole-issue serialization requirement. High-level invalid-scene guards are converter consumer integration, not ownership of prayer request scheduling or Hijri policy. The guard after eligible provider-zone adoption shares `runtime/day-adoption` with [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3), [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4), and [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5). Serialize those exact adoption/reinitialization hunks with their integrator; keep request, boot-day and promotion ownership distinct. This clarifies a write collision and adds no directed predecessor.

Change index.html's conversion and its necessary actual caller guards plus invoked regression fixtures. DESIGN must state the minute-precision domain, explicit unavailable gap/fold behavior and simulation error boundary; its old one-anchor description is revised jointly with the clock owner. Builder, config schema, presets and installers need no change. No active IMPLEMENTAUDIT controller/state, provider, dependency or deployment is involved.

Rollback converter/profile and dependent validity guards together if valid scenes, weather/current observation independence or countdown callers regress. A NaN-returning converter with unguarded consumers is an unsafe partial state. Completion requires final-tree RED→GREEN/control results, exact-tree independent caller review and browser clock/error/recovery readback before the evidence comment and manual #8 closure; use non-closing `Implements #8`. Public repair claims additionally require matching served source/readback. The historical companion remains supplementary, SHA256 `81ec493202ee83b988415f2d2608a1fc43464111ae21f27a38ddee8e36197dc4`; no new runtime result is claimed here.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.
